basis: Characteristic rib/thoracic dysplasia and developmental delay (80-99%); respiratory failure reflects thoracic restriction; pulmonary hypoplasia occurs in only 5-29%.

decisions.pulmonary: none: respiratory failure in 30-79% reflects thoracic restriction; direct pulmonary hypoplasia is reported in only 5-29%.

basis: Cerebellar ataxia, atrophy and pyramidal dysfunction define disease; frequent pes planus does not establish damaging skeletal involvement.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: pes planus occurs in 30-79%, but functional skeletal damage is not established; hypotonia and gait abnormalities reflect neurologic disease.

basis: Myotonic myopathy and skeletal dysplasia define disease; blepharophimosis in 1/3 does not establish impaired eyelid or visual function.

decisions.ocular: none: blepharophimosis is reported in 1/3, but narrowing alone does not demonstrate damaging eyelid dysfunction; cataract frequency is unspecified.

basis: Vertebral/rib ossification defects define disease; renal cysts and myelomeningocele each occur in 80-99%; pulmonary hypoplasia frequency is unspecified.

decisions.pulmonary: none: respiratory distress occurs in 80-99%, but may reflect thoracic restriction; direct pulmonary hypoplasia is not established at >=30%.

basis: Inherited PRNP-related cerebral prion deposition causes progressive ataxia and dementia; the usual disease arises through inherited protein misfolding.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: inherited PRNP-related prion formation defines this disease; potential transmissibility does not establish infection in the usual affected patient.

basis: Renal dysplasia, encephalocele and limb malformations define phenotype; hepatic ductal-plate malformation/fibrosis occurs in most Meckel cases (>30%); subtype data are sparse.

decisions.hepatic: involved: hepatic ductal-plate malformation with fibrosis occurs in most Meckel syndrome cases (>30%); this subtype has no established exception.

basis: Motor neuron degeneration, progressive skeletal-muscle atrophy and diaphragmatic paralysis define disease; eventration in 11/11. Respiratory failure is neuromuscular.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: progressive muscle atrophy and diaphragmatic paralysis are defining manifestations explicitly included in the disease definition; eventration occurred in 11/11.

basis: Cytochrome b5 deficiency causes methemoglobinemia and impaired androgen steroidogenesis; low DHEAS and elevated LH were documented in 1/1.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: impaired androgen steroidogenesis is an intrinsic biochemical defect of cytochrome b5 deficiency, supported by low DHEAS and elevated LH in 1/1.

basis: Congenital hepatic injury/failure; coagulopathy (7/14) reflects hepatic dysfunction. Anemia (5/14) and hypoglycemia (5/14) do not establish direct extrahepatic damage.

decisions.haematologic: none: coagulopathy (7/14) reflects hepatic synthetic dysfunction; nonspecific anemia (5/14) and splenomegaly do not establish direct blood-organ damage.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia (5/14) does not establish direct endocrine damage; a separately diagnosed hypoglycemic disorder is not added.

basis: Mitochondrial carrier deficiency causes epileptic encephalopathy; jejunal atresia and right ventricular hypertrophy each occur in 1/2 annotated patients (50%); sampling is sparse.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: structural right ventricular hypertrophy is reported in 1/2 annotated patients (50%); supplied HPO frequency supports inclusion despite the small sample.
decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: jejunal atresia directly disrupts intestinal structure and function and is reported in 1/2 annotated patients (50%); the small sample limits confidence.
